sections.content: Temporal connectors help a listener follow a memory without losing the order or the change over time. Use *al poco tiempo* for a later event, *a medida que* for a gradual change, *desde entonces* for a consequence that continues to the present, and *cuanto más …, más …* for two changes that grow together.

items.spanish: Al poco tiempo, volvimos al lugar donde había empezado la conversación.
items.english: Shortly afterwards, we returned to the place where the conversation had begun.

items.spanish: A medida que crecíamos, entendíamos mejor por qué mi madre guardaba aquellas cartas.
items.english: As we grew up, we understood better why my mother kept those letters.

items.spanish: Desde entonces, llamo a mi tío cuando una noticia me preocupa.
items.english: Since then, I call my uncle when some news worries me.

items.spanish: Al principio no nos conocíamos, pero al poco tiempo éramos buenos amigos.
items.english: At first we did not know each other, but shortly afterwards we were good friends.

sections.content: *Cuanto más …, más …* ("the more …, the more …") also links two changes, like *a medida que*, but says that the second grows with the first: *Cuanto más estudio, más entiendo.* Use *menos* for the opposite direction (*cuanto menos duermo, más cansado estoy*) and *mejor* or *peor* instead of *más bueno* or *más malo* (*cuanto más practico, mejor hablo*). *Cuanto* does not change when a verb follows it.

items.english: The more I study, the more I understand.
The more I practised, the better I spoke.

items.spanish: Cuanto menos duermo, más cansado estoy.
items.english: The less I sleep, the more tired I am.

sections.content: A connector should show a real relationship between clauses; do not add one merely to make a sentence longer.
